biography: Pietro Rimbano, a name once whispered with a mix of awe and trepidation in the Brazilian racing scene, emerged from the favelas of São Paulo with a burning desire to escape the confines of poverty. His first taste of speed came from illegally modified mopeds, dodging police patrols and weaving through the chaotic streets. This reckless abandon caught the eye of a local mechanic, who saw raw talent beneath the surface. The mechanic scraped together enough parts and funding for Pietro to enter a regional karting series. His aggressive style and never-say-die attitude quickly made him a fan favorite, but also a magnet for controversy. After a few years tearing up the regional scene he eventually made the jump to formula racing. A move to Box 99 Racing revitalized his career briefly, but now, at 37, the spark seems to be fading, and whispers of retirement are growing louder.
drivingStyle: Rimbano's driving style is characterized by relentless aggression. He attacks corners with a 'brake late, pray harder' philosophy, often pushing his car and tires beyond their limits. Tire management is not his forte; he prefers short bursts of blistering pace, sacrificing long-term consistency for immediate gains. Under pressure, he tends to become even more erratic, sometimes resulting in spectacular overtakes, other times ending in costly crashes. He thrives on chaos, often creating it himself.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision in the Brazilian Stock Car series that cost Vargas the championship.
A clash of personalities and driving styles, with Rossi often criticizing Rimbano's aggressive tactics as reckless and dangerous.
Battles on the track that sometimes ended with crashed cars, fueling a rivalry marked by mutual respect and animosity.

quirks: Always wears the same faded yellow t-shirt under his racing suit, a gift from his late grandmother.
Refuses to start a race without drinking a shot of strong Brazilian coffee mixed with a pinch of salt.
Tapes a small religious charm to his steering wheel before every session, a reminder of his humble beginnings.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Stock Car Championship in 2018 after a season-long battle with his arch-rival, Ricardo Vargas. The final race came down to the last corner, with Rimbano executing a daring overtake to secure the title.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Interlagos Grand Prix in 2021, costing him a potential victory on home soil and severely damaging his reputation.
